title: Timed-out child with stderr-only output loses diagnostics

answer.patch:
--- a/util/subprocess_timeout.py
+++ b/util/subprocess_timeout.py
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ def subprocess_with_hard_timeout(
         proc.wait(timeout=10)
         stdout = e.stdout if e.stdout else ""
         stderr = e.stderr if e.stderr else ""
-        if str(stdout).strip():
+        if str(stdout).strip() or str(stderr).strip():
             return subprocess.CompletedProcess(
                 args=cmd,
                 returncode=-9,
answer.reason: The bug is on line 59: the condition `if str(stdout).strip():` only checks stdout. When a subprocess writes only to stderr (no stdout), this evaluates to False and raises ProcTimeout instead of returning a CompletedProcess with stderr diagnostics. The fix changes the condition to check both stdout and stderr, ensuring stderr output is preserved even when stdout is empty.
